Noticed while attempting to reproduce the scene in the MRP that the root cannot be *any* Container as claimed. Plain Containers will not cause the freeze, and nor do certain other types like CenterContainer, but PanelContainer and MarginContainer seem to cause it. May be anecdotal.

Simply having the combination present in the scene will not freeze the editor initially, but will freeze it when opening the project again if the bugged scene is part of the previously opened scenes.

This is my first time trying to contribute to the source, so I know little. The code in commit \[[`aa094e9`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/aa094e93e36d9c310d0f40c466f0e063b7a7c9d4)\] appears to run without issue often in other situations. Maybe the call to `vscroll->get_bound_minimum_size()` is causing an undesirable side effect here?

`Godot v4.8.dev (2f2a9f4cc) - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:51:19 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 15.01 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)`

Can replicate even without `p_width > vscroll->get_bound_minimum_size().width` when changing the `Control` minimum width to exactly `30`. In this case it also takes way longer to crash. `_update_scroll_exceeds` parameters oscillate between two states:

I did some code tracing here, @TheDying0fLight's comment is very insightful.

This is a nasty cyclic reaction, that only works out because of particular timing.
Label Width -> Label Height -> Container Height -> TextureRect Width -> Label Width

| Chain 1 | Chain 2 |
|--------|--------|
| RTL sets its Height to 253 |  |
| Container syncs Height to 253 | Container sets RTL.width to 262|
| TextureRect sets its Width to 253 |  |
| Container sets RTL.width to 9 | RTL sets RTL.height to 23 |
| | Container syncs height to 23 | 
| | TextureRect sets its width to 23 |
| RTL sets RTL.height to 253 | Container sets RTL.width to 239 | 
| Container syncs Height to 253 | |
| TextureRect sets its Width to 253 | |
| Container sets RTL.Width to 9 | RTL sets RTL.height to 23 |
| And so on... | And so on... |

This only works out because the Container's update to the RTL's width and the RTL's update to its own height are processed in similar steps, before the next call to `_update_scroll_exceeds`, always triggering another resize event. This is why it does not stabilize on either valid configuration of the RTL (9, 253) or (239, 23)

My first suggestion for a fix would be to disable the Fit Content setting on a RichTextLabel when its size is controlled by a container. It might break some compatibility, but I think the existing behavior is inconsistent and confusing. Even in Scenarios where this does not cause a crash, there are varying outcomes with similar inputs depending on order of operations, and other container elements getting 'locked' in a certain state. I found cases where CMD+Z correctly undid a change on a singular element, but put the overall container into a different state than it was initially.

**Edit:** That said, given DyingLights comment that you can recreate the crash even without https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/aa094e93e36d9c310d0f40c466f0e063b7a7c9d4 (Which I also verified by compiling the edit on 4.8 Master), I tested on older version of Godot 4, and could not recreate the crash on Godot 4.0, 4.5.1, or a 4.6 Beta build I had lying around. This would suggest that something else introduced the possibility of the cyclic behavior and there are better solutions than my first suggestion
